name: The Toll Roads (Orange County FasTrak - SR 73, 133, 241, 261)
notes: Tier 2. Researched from public thetollroads.com pages (home, Ways to Pay Tolls, Basics of FasTrak, violation FAQs). The payment-plan FAQ was read once via a page fetch; later direct fetches of FAQ pages hit a bot check that was not bypassed, so the account-management and statements FAQs and the secure portal's sign-in page (secure.thetollroads.com returned 404 to a plain fetch) were not read; sign-in wording, close-account steps and replenishment amounts keep the family defaults. FasTrak accounts: prepay tolls, charge each toll to a card, or pay by invoice; no monthly maintenance fees; monthly activity statements by email; frequent driver discounts. No account: pay online by license plate within 5 days before or after driving (tolls can take 48 hours to appear). Violations: $57.50 penalty per violation plus the toll; second notice adds $42.50; DMV registration hold after the second notice. Payment plans for toll evasion notices are created online with the reference and violation numbers; the low-income plan (CVC 40269.5: 200% of poverty guidelines, up to $2,500 owed) caps payments at $25 a month for amounts up to $600 and lifts DMV holds after the first payment. Cash via PayNearMe (convenience fee added by PayNearMe) or walk-in centers. Gift certificates from $15. Review 2026-10-10: Ways to Pay Tolls lists three FasTrak plans (Prepaid: no account fees, discounted tolls; Charge: no account fees; Invoice: $2 monthly invoice fee), so the 'no maintenance fees' wording was limited to prepaid/charge. Penalty, payment-plan and mail-payment FAQs re-read and confirmed.

autopay.note: With a FasTrak account, tolls are deducted from your prepaid balance or charged individually to the credit card on file.

paperless.note: Monthly activity statements are emailed to you.

guest_pay.note: No account? Pay tolls online with just your license plate number within 5 days before or after you drive.

payment_arrangement.note: If you cannot pay a toll violation in full, set up a payment plan with your reference and violation numbers. Income-eligible drivers owing $2,500 or less pay no more than $25 a month on amounts up to $600.

help.title: Paying tolls without an account
paragraphs: Drivers without a FasTrak account can pay a toll online up to 5 days before or after driving The Toll Roads; all you need is the license plate number. Tolls can take up to 48 hours to post to a plate, so check back if you drove recently.
You can also pay with cash at a Customer Service Walk-In Center or through PayNearMe at participating retailers such as 7-Eleven, CVS and Walmart; PayNearMe adds its own convenience fee.

help.title: Toll violation penalties
paragraphs: If you have no account and do not pay within 5 days before or after driving, a violation is issued for each trip with a $57.50 penalty on top of the toll.
Ignoring the first notice brings a second notice with another $42.50 penalty, and an unanswered second notice can lead to a DMV hold on the vehicle registration.
Pay violations on the Toll Violation page, in The Toll Roads app, by check to The Toll Roads Violations Dept., PO Box 57011, Irvine, CA 92618, or with cash at a walk-in center or PayNearMe.

help.title: Violation payment plans
paragraphs: If you cannot pay a toll evasion notice in full, create a payment plan in the secure account and payment portal with your reference number and violation number.

Under California's low-income program, drivers at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines who owe $2,500 or less can pay no more than $25 a month on amounts up to $600, and DMV holds are lifted after the first payment. Bring proof such as CalFresh or Medi-Cal enrollment, a county benefits letter or a recent tax return to the Irvine or Rancho Cucamonga walk-in center.

help.title: FasTrak account options
paragraphs: A FasTrak account with The Toll Roads lets you prepay tolls, charge them to a card, or pay by invoice. Prepaid and charge accounts have no account fees (prepaid accounts also get discounted tolls); invoice accounts pay a $2 monthly invoice fee. Activity statements are emailed monthly, and frequent drivers may qualify for discounts.
Every vehicle on the account needs a properly mounted transponder. Gift certificates from $15 can fund a new or existing account.
